questions.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x+y?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 \\ 0.6x-0.8y=1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 &  \\ 0.6x-0.8y=1 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 \\ 6x-8y=10\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $3$ and the second equation by $-2,$ we will get a $12x$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-12x$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x+3y=15 & |\,\times 3 \\ 6x-8y=10 & |\,\times -2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}12x+9y=45 \\ -12x+16y=-20\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{12x}+9y & =45 \\ -\cancel{12x}+16y & =-20 \\ (9y+16y) & =(45-20) \\ 25y & =25 \\ y & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=1$ into the equation $4x+3y=15$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+3y & =15 \\ 4x+3 & =15 \\ 4x & =15-3 \\ 4x & =12 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=3$ and $y=1.$ So, 

$$
x+y=3+1=4.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the solution of the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}b=2a-1 \\ 1.5a+0.5b=2.5\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}b=2a-1 &  \\ 1.5a+0.5b=2.5 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}b=2a-1 \\ 15a+5b=25\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the first equation is already solved for $b:$

$$
b=2a-1
$$

Now, to find the value of $a,$ we can substitute $b=2a-1$ into the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}15a+5(2a-1) & =25 \\ 15a+10a-5 & =25 \\ 25a & =30 \\ a & =\frac{30}{25} \\ a & =1.2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $a=1.2$ into the  first equation to get:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =2(1.2)-1 \\  & =2.4-1 \\  & =1.4\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=1.2$ and $b=1.4.$

questions.problem:
Find the solution of the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}12.8a+6.4=-6.4b \\ 2a+1=b\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}12.8a+6.4=-6.4b & |\,\times 10 \\ 2a+1=b & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}128a+64=-64b \\ 2a+1=b\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the second equation is already solved for $b:$

$$
b=2a+1
$$

Now, to find the value of $a,$ we can substitute $b=2a+1$ into the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}128a+64 & =-64b \\ 128a+64 & =-64(2a+1) \\ 128a+64 & =-128a-64 \\ 256a & =-128 \\ a & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ a & =-0.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $a=-0.5$ into the second equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+1 & =b \\ 2(-0.5)+1 & =b \\ -1+1 & =b \\ b & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-0.5$ and $b=0.$

questions.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x+y?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=7 \\ 0.5x+0.4y=0.2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=7 &  \\ 0.5x+0.4y=0.2 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x+3y=7 \\ 5x+4y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the  first equation by $-5,$ then we will get a $-5x$ term that can cancel with the $5x$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=7 & |\,\times (-5) \\ 5x+4y=2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}-5x-15y=-35 \\ 5x+4y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}-\cancel{5x}-15y & =-35 \\ \cancel{5x}+4y & =2 \\ (-15y+4y) & =(-33) \\ -11y & =-33 \\ y & =3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=3$ into the equation $x+3y=7$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}x+3y & =7 \\ x+3(3) & =7 \\ x+9 & =7 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=-2,\,y=3.$ So,

$$
x+y=(-2)+(3)=1.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $(x,y)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $x-y?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2.3x+4.6y=69 \\ 10x-20y=100\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the top equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2.3x+4.6y=69 & |\,\times 10 \\ 10x-20y=100 & \end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}23x+46y=690 \\ 10x-20y=100\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we divide the first equation by $23$ and the second equation by $10,$ we will get a $2y$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-2y$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}23x+46y=690 & |\,÷23 \\ 10x-20y=100 & |\,÷10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x+2y=30 \\ x-2y=10\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable and allows us to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\cancel{2y} & =30 \\ x-\cancel{2y} & =10 \\ (x+x) & =(30+10) \\ 2x & =40 \\ x & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $x=20$ into the equation $x+2y=30$ to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & =30 \\ (20)+2y & =30 \\ 2y & =30-20 \\ 2y & =10 \\ y & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=20$ and $y=5.$ So, 

$$
x-y=20-(5)=15.
$$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.3x-0.1y=0.6 \\ 0.6x+0.8y=0.2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.3x-0.1y=0.6 & |\,\times 10 \\ 0.6x+0.8y=0.2 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3x-y=6 \\ 6x+8y=2\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we divide the second equation by $(-2),$ we will get a $-3x$ term in the second equation that can cancel with the $3x$ term in the first equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-y=6 &  \\ 6x+8y=2 & |\,÷(-2)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}3x-y=6 \\ -3x-4y=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable and allows us to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{3x}-y & =6 \\ -\cancel{3x}-4y & =-1 \\ (-y-4y) & =(6-1) \\ -5y & =5 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $y=-1$ into the equation $3x-y=6$ to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-y & =6 \\ 3x-(-1) & =6 \\ 3x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $x=\frac{5}{3}$ and $y=-1.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.09v-0.04w=0.05 \\ 0.02v-0.01w=0.2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $100,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.09v-0.04w=0.05 & |\times 100 \\ 0.02v-0.01w=0.2 & |\times 100\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}9v-4w=5 \\ 2v-w=20\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we multiply the second equation by $-4,$ we will get a $4w$ term that can cancel with the $-4w$ term in the first equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}9v-4w=5 &  \\ 2v-w=20 & |\,\times (-4)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}9v-4w=5 \\ -8v+4w=-80\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $w$-variable and allows us to solve for $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}9v-\cancel{4w} & =5 \\ -8v+\cancel{4w} & =-80 \\ (9v-8v) & =(5-80) \\ v & =-75\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $v=-75$ into the equation $2v-w=20$ to solve for $w:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2v-w & =20 \\ 2(-75)-w & =20 \\ -150-w & =20 \\ -w & =170 \\ w & =-170\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $v=-75,\,w=-170.$

questions.problem:
Let $(p,q)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $p+2q?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.36p+1.2q=0.36 \\ -1.9p-7.6q=3.8\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equation by $100$ and the second equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.36p+1.2q=0.36 & |\times 100 \\ -1.9p-7.6q=3.8 & |\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}36p+120q=36 \\ -19p-76q=38\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can solve for $p$ in the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-19p-76q & =38 \\ -19p & =76q+38 \\ p & =\frac{76q+38}{-19} \\ p & =-4q-2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the value of $q,$ we can substitute $p=-4q-2$ into the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}36p+120q & =36 \\ 36(-4q-2)+120q & =36 \\ -144q-72+120q & =36 \\ -24q & =108 \\ q & =-\frac{108}{24} \\ q & =-4.5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $q=-4.5$ into the equation $p=-4q-2$ to get:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =-4q-2 \\ p & =-4(-4.5)-2 \\ p & =18-2 \\ p & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=16$ and $q=-4.5.$ So, 

$$
p+2q=16+2(-4.5)=16-9=7.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $(a,b)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $a+b?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}a+1.5b-6=0 \\ 0.6a-0.4b-1=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}a+1.5b-6=0 & |\,\times 10 \\ 0.6a-0.4b-1=0 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}10a+15b-60=0 \\ 6a-4b-10=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we  multiply the first equation by $\frac{2}{5}$ and the second equation by $\frac{3}{2},$ we will get a $6b$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-6b$ term in the second equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}10a+15b-60=0 & |\,\times \frac{2}{5} \\ 6a-4b-10=0 & |\,\times \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}4a+6b-24=0 \\ 9a-6b-15=0\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $b$-variable and allows us to solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4a+\cancel{6b}-24 & =0 \\ 9a-\cancel{6b}-15 & =0 \\ (4a+9a)+(-24-15) & =0 \\ 13a-39 & =0 \\ a & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $a=3$ into the equation $6a-4b-10=0$ to solve for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6a-4b-10 & =0 \\ 6(3)-4b-10 & =0 \\ 18-4b-10 & =0 \\ 8-4b & =0 \\ b & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=3$ and $b=2.$ So, 

$$
a+b=3+2=5.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $(v,w)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $v+w?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.5v-2.5w=7.5 \\ 0.7v+0.3w=2.9\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.5v-2.5w=7.5 & |\times 10 \\ 0.7v+0.3w=2.9 & |\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}5v-25w=75 \\ 7v+3w=29\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can solve for $v$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5v-25w & =75 \\ 5v & =25w+75 \\ v & =\frac{25w+75}{5} \\ v & =5w+15\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the value of $w,$ we can substitute $v=5w+15$ into the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}7v+3w & =29 \\ 7(5w+15)+3w & =29 \\ 35w+105+3w & =29 \\ 38w & =-76 \\ w & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $w=-2$ into the equation $v=5w+15$ to get:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =5w+15 \\ v & =5(-2)+15 \\ v & =-10+15 \\ v & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $v=5,\,w=-2.$ So,

$$
v+w=5+(-2)=3.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.5x+3y+4=0 \\ 4x=-20y-20\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equation by $10,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0.5x+3y+4=0 & |\,\times 10 \\ 4x=-20y-20 & \end{aligned}
$$

We also notice that each equation can be simplified by dividing by a common factor. In the first equation, the common factor is $5,$ while in the second equation, the common factor is $4.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x+30y+40=0 & |\,÷5 \\ 4x=-20y-20 & |\,÷4\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the second equation is already solved for $x.$ So, we can substitute $x = -5y-5$ into the first equation and then solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+6y+8 & =0 \\ (-5y-5)+6y+8 & =0 \\ y+3 & =0 \\ y & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=-3$ back into $x=-5y-5,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-5y-5 \\  & =-5(-3)-5 \\  & =15-5 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x = 10$ and $y = -3,$ which can be expressed as $(10, -3).$

canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}1.4x+2.8y=1.4 \\ 0.02x+0.01y=0.05\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply the first equation by $10$ and the second equation by $100,$ as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}1.4x+2.8y=1.4 & |\times 10 \\ 0.02x+0.01y=0.05 & |\times 100\end{aligned}
$$

To simplify the first equation, we divide by $14\mathbin{:}$

$$
{\begin{aligned}14x+28y=14 & |÷14 \\ 2x+y=5\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the first equation can easily be solved for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2y & =1 \\ x & =1-2y\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can substitute $x=1-2y$ into the second equation and then solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y & =5 \\ 2(1-2y)+y & =5 \\ 2-4y+y & =5 \\ 2-3y & =5 \\ -3y & =3 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=-1$ back into $x=1-2y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =1-2y \\  & =1-2(-1) \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x =3$ and $y =-1$, which can be expressed as $(3, -1).$
